prize_parts.citation: for the physiology of the incretin hormone GLP-1 and its development into long-acting therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: All six openings placed GLP-1 first, and I agree that it is the strongest case on the shortlist. It is a continuous chain from hormone physiology (proglucagon processing, the insulinotropic and satiety actions of GLP-1, receptor biology) to long-acting agonists with robust randomized-trial evidence in diabetes, obesity and cardiorenal outcomes. The mechanism is settled, independently confirmed and in very wide clinical use, so the timing is right. A prize that credits both the physiology (Drucker, Holst) and the step that made it a durable drug (Knudsen) captures the full discovery-to-therapy arc, which is what distinguishes this candidate from the method-oriented ones on the list.
statement.case_against: The credit is the weak point. Four credited names do not fit in three seats, and any trio omits someone whose claim is serious. If Knudsen is excluded, the prize drops the pharmacological step that produced liraglutide and semaglutide. If Mojsov is excluded, the prize risks looking like it ignores a contested but real contribution to identifying the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide. Habener, who is not on the credited list, complicates the priority question further. Unanimous opening support also reflects a shared view of impact, not a settled view of attribution, and the committee should not mistake one for the other.

responses.point: Knudsen's work is drug development that sits more naturally in an industry setting, so Holst, Drucker and Mojsov are the strongest scientific trio.
responses.response: I take the argument that the prize should reward discovery first, but I do not think industry setting is a principled exclusion. The step from a peptide with a minutes-long half-life to a once-weekly agonist was a conceptual and technical advance in its own right, and it is the reason the physiology reached patients at scale. The medical case for this prize rests on that translation. I would exclude Knudsen only if the committee is convinced that Mojsov's contribution to the active peptide is decisive and uncontested, and I do not think the supplied evidence shows that.

responses.point: Mojsov identified the active peptide form and its insulinotropic action, supporting a three-person physiology-weighted configuration, while Knudsen is an industrial contributor left out to stay within three.
responses.response: This is the most serious competing configuration, and I am not certain mine is better. Where I differ is on how much weight priority for the peptide sequence and structure should carry compared with showing that the peptide could be made into a long-lasting drug. You note yourself that Mojsov's priority relative to other early contributors is contested and cannot be verified from the supplied text. A contested claim is a risky basis for the one seat that decides the configuration. I would revisit this if the committee can verify the primary record of who first demonstrated the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36) amide.

responses.point: Optogenetics is an enabling invention of broad lasting impact, but the three-person cap cannot reflect all of Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck, so the choice of Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann is contestable.
responses.response: I agree with the diagnosis and it is why I keep optogenetics as an alternative and not as my preferred configuration. A trio of Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann leaves out Boyden on the neuronal demonstration, and I see no principled way to separate Deisseroth from Boyden and Miesenböck on the supplied evidence. It is also a method award, which the committee should weigh against disease-relevant discoveries. I would not let the strong opening ranks of B005 push it above B008, where the credit problem is smaller.

responses.point: The GLP-1 bench-to-bedside arc is exceptional, but Knudsen is the fourth name and her contribution may be judged equal to the others.
responses.response: We agree on the strength of the case and on the fact that Knudsen's contribution is equal in weight to the other names. We differ on who gives way. Since you accept her contribution may be decisive, I read that as an argument for including her, and for treating the seat that Mojsov would take as the real open question. I would welcome a discussion of whether a two-part framing, discovery plus development, makes the citation cleaner than a single physiology citation.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov or Knudsen should hold the third seat, and whether the primary record can resolve Mojsov's priority relative to Habener and others.
Whether the citation should be framed as physiology only or as physiology plus drug development.
For B008, whether Eshhar and other early CAR originators outside the credited names make that credit configuration incomplete.
Long-term safety and durability of chronic incretin therapy are still accumulating.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for the shortlisted candidates. My Karolinska Institutet affiliation and my spatial transcriptomics co-authorship are unrelated to the credited names on the shortlist, and I do not infer any personal connection from shared institutions.
